GENERATED by tools/research_domains.py --build. Every committed research domain, its reading-unit patterns and stable unit-id rule. Hand-edit and the gate says so.

RECORD-ID SCOPE (T-1338). A ledger unit's key in tools/research_spend_ledger.py is its row id, and two corpora here reuse a row id across their own files while meaning opposite things by it: a residents pass cohort names the same man in four passes, and a newspaper issue numbers its claims from c001 with no reference to any other issue. Nothing in the id tells them apart, so each container whose ids repeat says which it is. `file_local_containers` means the key is the source file's stem and the id joined by `#` — `chicago_democrat_1835_08_19#c007`, the form the resident cards' own notes already wrote — and a card must name that whole form to spend such a unit. `global_containers` means the id is a name the whole corpus agrees on and the bare id is the key. An undeclared repeat is a fault: taking it for global silently is what closed 145 units as asserted off three cards that had each cited exactly one claim.

domains.title: Civic lists
domains.what: The town's own lists of its own people — the poll books and voter rolls of 1833-1835, and the officers, jurors and subscribers printed beside them.

ledger_units.record_ids_note: Same numbering as the papers', and this domain's c013 collided with the Democrat's across the two of them.

domains.title: The 1830 federal census
domains.what: Chicago was enumerated in Peoria County in 1830. The named schedule is the object; the county aggregates this project already holds are not it.

domains.title: The 1840 federal census
domains.what: Seventy-five page images and a head-of-household index. 1840 is LATER EVIDENCE and never an 1835 household fact on its own.

ledger_units.record_ids_note: These rows carry no id at all, so the key falls back to the file-relative JSON pointer /records/0, which every sheet has.

domains.title: Church registers
domains.what: Baptisms, marriages and burials — St Mary's 1833-1835 first, because eleven images of its register are already deposited and unread.

domains.title: Books and reminiscences
domains.what: Prose: Fergus' Historical Series, Hubbard's autobiography, H. H. Porter's Short Autobiography, and the memoirs printed beside them.

domains.title: Directories
domains.what: The 1839 Chicago directory and its successors — entry by entry, structured, and crosswalked rather than quoted at second hand.

domains.title: Federal land tract sales
domains.what: The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales database, read for the townships around Chicago through 1836. A sale is a transaction, never a residence; the register's own Residence column is the only thing here that speaks to where a purchaser lived.

domains.title: The Calumet Club's old settlers
domains.what: The rolls of the Calumet Club's receptions to the old settlers of Chicago (1879-1882) and the obituary list printed in Fergus's 1843 directory. Every one of them is LATER EVIDENCE about a person, and the obituary list's own header admits it also names citizens who arrived after 1843 — so a name here is never an 1835 residence.

domains.title: The Newberry genealogical index
domains.what: A four-volume photostat of the Newberry Library's genealogical card index (G. K. Hall, 1960), read for the cards whose citation names Chicago, Cook County or Illinois. A card says where a genealogy IS; it never places a person, and nothing here may grade one.

domains.title: Genealogy Trails transcriptions
domains.what: Hand-read transcriptions of Chicago church and civic records; a later primary-source reading may supersede a claim but never erase it.

domains.title: Chicago newspapers
domains.what: Claims read from the committed Chicago Democrat and Chicago American corpus; gazetteers and registers are generated from these units.

ledger_units.record_ids_note: A claim id is a position in the extraction of ONE issue; 55 issue files each print c001, and the ledger key is therefore the file's stem and the id joined by `#`.

domains.title: Resident research passes
domains.what: Named resident cohorts and focused audits whose positive and negative findings must survive regeneration of the public resident cards.

ledger_units.record_ids_note: A person id is the person. The pass cohorts are cohorts of one town and 225 people are read by more than one of them, so the bare id is the key and must stay so.
